The '''2026 SANFL season''' (officially known as the '''SANFL [[Hostplus]] League''' for sponsorship reasons) was the 147th season of the [[South Australian National Football League]] (SANFL), the highest-level men's [[Australian rules football]] competition in [[South Australia]].<ref>{{cite web|url=https://sanfl.com.au/league/news/2026-hostplus-sanfl-league-fixture-release/|title=2026 Hostplus SANFL League Fixture Released|work=sanfl.com.au|date=10 December 2025|author=Zac Milbank}}</ref> The season commenced on 27 March and concluded on 20 September.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.adelaidenow.com.au/subscribe/news/1/?sourceCode=AAWEB_WRE170_a_GGL&dest=https%3A%2F%2Fwww.adelaidenow.com.au%2Fsport%2Fsanfl-season-to-begin-with-a-bang-as-flag-favourites-sturt-and-norwood-go-headtohead-at-the-parade%2Fnews-story%2F41587dfcd79038d092d865d24ca432ec&memtype=anonymous&mode=premium&v21=HIGH-Segment-2-SCORE|title=SANFL Fixture Reveal: Blockbuster start to 2026 season|work=The Advertiser|date=10 December 2025|url-access=subscription}}</ref>

{{SANFL Nor}} won the [[List of SANFL premiers|premiership]] for the 32nd time, defeating {{SANFL Stu}} by 14 points in the [[2026 SANFL Grand Final|Grand Final]]. It was the club's second premiership of the decade and brought them within four titles of the record held by {{SANFL Por}}. 

==Background==
The 2026 season marked the 147th season of the competition and the fourth since the competition's return to a full 18-game home-and-away season following the [[COVID-19 pandemic]]. The competition continued to consist of ten clubs, including the [[Australian Football League reserves affiliations|reserves teams]] of [[Adelaide Football Club|Adelaide]] and [[Port Adelaide Football Club|Port Adelaide]]. The top five teams at the conclusion of the home-and-away season qualified for the finals series, which culminated in the grand final at [[Adelaide Oval]].

{{SANFL Stu}} entered the season as reigning premiers, having defeated [[Glenelg Football Club|Glenelg]] by 31 points in the [[2025 SANFL Grand Final|2025 grand final]] to deny the Bays the opportunity to become the first SANFL club to record three consecutive premierships since the 1950's.<ref>{{cite web |title=Sturt win 2025 Hostplus SANFL League Premiership |url=https://sanfl.com.au/league/news/sturt-win-2025-hostplus-sanfl-league-premiership/ |work=sanfl.com.au|date=22 September 2025}}</ref> Four clubs entered the 2026 season with new senior coaches. [[West Adelaide Football Club|West Adelaide]] appointed former Norwood premiership coach [[Nathan Bassett]], while [[North Adelaide Football Club|North Adelaide]], Glenelg and Port Adelaide also appointed new senior coaches. Port Adelaide appointed [[Jacob Surjan]] to lead its SANFL side.<ref>{{cite web |title=Coaching elite primed for 2026 Hostplus SANFL League |url=https://sanfl.com.au/league/news/coaching-elite-primed-for-2026-hostplus-sanfl-league/ |website=SANFL |date=30 January 2026}}</ref><ref>{{cite web |title=Jacob Surjan to coach Port Adelaide’s SANFL team in 2026 |url=https://sanfl.com.au/league/news/jacob-surjan-to-coach-port-adelaides-sanfl-team-in-2026/ |website=SANFL |date=24 October 2025}}</ref>

==Representative matches==
===SANFL vs VFL===
For the third successive season, an [[Interstate matches in Australian rules football|interstate representative match]] was arranged against the [[Victorian Football League]] (VFL). As was the case with the [[2025 SANFL season#SANFL vs VFL|2025 fixture]], the match was timed to coincide with the AFL's [[Gather Round]] fixtures in Adelaide. The match was held as part of a double-header with the equivalent women's interstate match.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.sportingnews.com/au/afl/news/state-leagues-exhibition-games-set-afl-gather-round-2026-vfl-sanfl/afda5fa97995154a901bf8ec|title=State leagues exhibition games set for AFL Gather Round 2026|work=The Sporting News|date=10 December 2025|author=Jake Beddard|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20251222063823/https://www.sportingnews.com/au/afl/news/state-leagues-exhibition-games-set-afl-gather-round-2026-vfl-sanfl/afda5fa97995154a901bf8ec|archive-date=22 December 2025|url-status=live}}</ref>

===WAFL vs SANFL===
For the eighth successive season, an interstate representative match was fixtured between the SANFL and [[West Australian Football League]] (WAFL), with the two teams playing for the [[Haydn Bunton Jr.|Haydn Bunton Junior]] Cup.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://sanfl.com.au/league/news/2026-hostplus-sanfl-league-fixture-release/|title=2026 Hostplus SANFL League Fixture Released|date=24 December 2025|work=sanfl.com.au|quote=The West End State team will have its sights set on regaining the Haydn Bunton Junior Cup in the KIA State Game against the WAFL on the weekend of Saturday May 16 after it hosts the VFL at Stratarama Stadium on Saturday April 11 as part of the AFL Gather Round festivities.|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20260201040856/https://sanfl.com.au/league/news/2026-hostplus-sanfl-league-fixture-release/|archive-date=1 February 2026|url-status=live}}</ref><ref>{{cite web|url=https://wafootball.com.au/news/historic-kia-state-game-triple-header-locked-in/|title=Historic Kia State Game triple-header locked in|work=WA Football|date=17 April 2026|author=Jordan McArdle|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20260420033217/https://wafootball.com.au/news/historic-kia-state-game-triple-header-locked-in/|archive-date=20 April 2026|url-status=live}}</ref>
